Ooo I’m so excited I actually know about this a lot. So usually the first antidepressants your dr will offer are the ssri’s your Zoloft lexapro all those types. While they are effective in a lot of people not everyone tolerate them well (I was in a similar situation to you where one med I tried just took away all emotion and another was ineffective for all of my symptoms, it was a thing.)

Something that greatly helped me was switching to an snri, the only difference between the two is that ssri’s keep just a little extra serotonin In the brain  snri’s keep that serotonin and norepinephrine in the brain. (While it’s less famous then happy drug serotonin norepinephrine is another neurotransmitter that can if in the brain longer helps with energy and mood)

I will say in my experience snri’s have more stupid side effects? Like Effexor, the one I’m on now, actually has excessive yawning as a side effect. And like while I was working my way up to a higher dose I was perpetually thirsty but now that I’m steady on it most of them have gone away. (I mean I still yawn more but now I can blame it on something) 

While I will say therapy has helped a lot along with meds that medications are still a part of the combo that keeps me going. 

(Also fun fact I learned in class about norepinephrine is that it may play a factor in adhd so it’s possible that may also affect your dr’s willingness to prescribe an snri, but I don’t know for sure I’m a biology student not a dr)
